questions.prompt: He held the position as long as he could stand the work.
questions.answer: tenuit locum tamdiū quam ferre potuit labōrem.

questions.prompt: Our grandfather as long as he lived, opposed Gratidius.
questions.answer: avus noster quoad vīxit, restitit M. Grātidiō.

questions.prompt: As long as it had to be, and circumstances demanded, one man controlled the world.
questions.answer: dum necesse erat, rēsque ipsa cōgēbat, ūnus omnia poterat.

questions.prompt: As long as they were moving off under arms and in close array, the task of pursuit fell to the infantry.
questions.answer: dōnec armātī cōnfertīque abībant, peditum labor in persequendō fuit.

questions.prompt: The rank and file were butchered as long as wrath and daylight held out.
questions.answer: vulgus trucīdātum est dōnec īra et diēs permānsit.

questions.prompt: He stuck to his bargain till the jurors were challenged.
questions.answer: mānsit in condiciōne usque ad eum fīnem dum iūdicēs rēiectī sunt.

questions.prompt: I am thinking of staying here till I feel better.
questions.answer: ego hīc cōgitō commorārī, quoad mē reficiam.

questions.prompt: You will keep this back till I see you myself.
questions.answer: ea continēbis, quoad ipse tē videam.

questions.prompt: They always live among the same flocks and herds, till maturity puts the free-born by themselves.
questions.answer: inter eadem pecora dēgunt, dōnec aetās sēparet ingenuōs.

questions.prompt: Our people routed them and did not give up the pursuit till the cavalry drove the enemy headlong.
questions.answer: nostrī reppulērunt neque fīnem sequendī fēcērunt, quoad equitēs praecipitēs hostēs ēgērunt.

questions.prompt: I was afraid all the time till we came to challenging jurors.
questions.answer: usque eō timuī, dōnec ad rēiciundōs iūdicēs vēnimus.

questions.prompt: He used to practise running and wrestling, till he could give a grip standing.
questions.answer: exercēbātur currendō et lūctandō ad eum fīnem, quoad stāns complectī posset.
